topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cellular differentiation, genetic alterations, and tissue architecture in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the foundational concept of cancer as a progressive disruption of genetic regulation, cellular differentiation, and three-dimensional tissue organization, alongside the experimental limitations of cell culture models.

topics.label: Pathology of tumor invasion, metastasis, and malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the pathological processes and histological criteria that distinguish benign lesions from invasive and metastatic malignant tumors, illustrated through the stepwise adenoma-to-adenocarcinoma sequence.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and pathophysiological mechanisms of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the systematic naming conventions for different tumor types and explain the physiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant tumors cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine epidemiological patterns of tumor incidence in human populations and compare cancer occurrence across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how tumors present clinically and evaluate the histological principles, methodologies, and efficacy of screening programs for various cancers.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and housekeeping instructions for the next lecture and practical sessions.
